fatal_errors: The proposed second-phase/TRIP intervention does not reconstruct the thermal-aging intervention or the temperature-dependent ordering and phase-boundary evolution in the target.
The initial material is incorrectly treated as a single-phase solid solution, whereas the target alloy is an as-cast FCC+B2 eutectic HEA.
No exposure temperatures, durations, or loading regime are specified, so the proposed hypothesis cannot address the 550–750°C brittle window or the recovery near 750°C.
The predicted monotonic preservation of toughness misses the observed non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
The cited evidence supports general TRIP-enabled strength–ductility or cryogenic damage tolerance, not preservation of toughness after the relevant thermal aging.
Introducing a second phase does not by itself establish that a stress- or strain-induced phase transformation will occur during loading.
explanation: The response is only broadly aligned with the topic of improving mechanical performance in compositionally complex alloys. It replaces the relevant intervention—intermediate-temperature aging—with an unspecified introduction of a TRIP-capable second phase, and it omits the central mechanism involving enhanced L12 ordering, elevated antiphase-boundary energy, planar slip, dislocation pile-ups, and stress concentration at jagged FCC/B2 phase-boundary tips. It also fails to predict the minimum ductility near 600°C and recovery near 750°C. The proposed treated-versus-untreated comparison is testable at a basic level, but without defined temperatures, exposure times, phase fractions, transformation measurements, or loading conditions it cannot discriminate TRIP from ordinary second-phase strengthening. E1 provides limited general support for TRIP alloys, while E2 concerns single-phase CrCoNi damage tolerance at low temperature and does not support the claimed thermal-exposure mechanism.
